books.title: The Black Tulip
books.author: Alexandre Dumas
books.desc: In the Holland of 1672, a gentle tulip grower races to breed the first black tulip, but political murder, a jealous rival and prison stand in his way.
about: In August 1672, a furious crowd in The Hague turns on the brothers Johan and Cornelius de Witt, the former leaders of the Dutch Republic. Their quiet godson, Cornelius van Baerle, a wealthy young doctor, cares nothing for politics: his passion is tulips, and he hopes to win the great prize offered by the city of Haarlem for the first black tulip. His envious neighbour, Isaac Boxtel, spies on him day and night, and when Cornelius is thrown into prison, his only hope lies with Rosa, the jailer Gryphus's daughter.

Dumas combines a dramatic page of Dutch history with a tender love story and a tale of patience, rivalry and obsession. Shorter and more intimate than his great musketeer novels, it shows his gift for suspense and lively dialogue.

The Black Tulip was published in 1850, written with the collaboration of Auguste Maquet. It is set against the background of the Dutch passion for tulips. This edition offers the original French text and an English translation by an unnamed translator.

books.title: Michael Strogoff
books.author: Jules Verne
books.desc: The Tsar's courier must cross thousands of miles of Siberia, overrun by a Tartar invasion, to warn the Grand Duke in Irkutsk of a traitor's plot.
about: A Tartar rebellion led by Feofar Khan has cut Siberia off from Moscow, and the telegraph lines are down. The traitor Ivan Ogareff, a former colonel thirsting for revenge, plans to betray the city of Irkutsk, where the Tsar's brother is holding out. The Tsar sends Michael Strogoff, a courageous courier from Omsk, to carry a warning across thousands of miles of hostile land. On the way he meets Nadia, a young woman travelling to join her exiled father, and two rival war correspondents, Harry Blount and Alcide Jolivet.

Verne writes a breathless adventure across rivers, steppes and forests, full of danger, disguise and endurance, and paints a vast picture of nineteenth-century Russia and Siberia. Loyalty, courage and love are tested at every step.

Michael Strogoff was published by Pierre-Jules Hetzel in 1876 as one of Verne's Extraordinary Voyages. It has been adapted many times for the stage and screen. This edition offers the original French text, an English translation and a German translation, both by unnamed translators.

books.title: The Mystery of the Yellow Room
books.author: Gaston Leroux
books.desc: A woman is attacked inside a room locked from within, and the attacker has vanished; a brilliant young reporter takes on France's top detective to solve it.
about: At the Château du Glandier, the scientist Professor Stangerson and his daughter Mathilde work on their research. One night, cries and shots are heard from the Yellow Room, where Mathilde sleeps. When the door, locked and bolted from the inside, is broken down, she is found gravely wounded, and the attacker has disappeared. The young journalist Joseph Rouletabille, eighteen years old and full of confidence, sets out to solve the case against the famous detective Frédéric Larsan, while Mathilde's fiancé, Robert Darzac, behaves strangely.

Leroux builds an ingenious puzzle around an apparently impossible crime, with plans of the château, clues and reasoning laid before the reader, and adds humour, suspense and a mysterious past. Rouletabille became one of the great detectives of French fiction.

The Mystery of the Yellow Room was first published in the magazine L'Illustration from September to November 1907 and as a book in 1908. It is one of the first and most famous locked-room mysteries. This edition offers the original French text and an English translation by an unnamed translator.

books.title: Manon Lescaut
books.author: Abbé Prévost
books.desc: A young nobleman destined for the Church gives up everything for the charming, unreliable Manon, in one of the great love stories of French literature.

editions.credit: Traduction : Antonio de Hoyos y Vinent (1885-1940)

about: A man of quality meets a young nobleman, the Chevalier des Grieux, escorting a group of women condemned to be deported, and later hears his story. At seventeen, about to enter the Church, des Grieux met the beautiful Manon Lescaut at an inn in Amiens, where she was being sent to a convent, and ran away with her to Paris. Torn between his love for Manon, who cannot bear poverty, and the advice of his loyal friend Tiberge, he is drawn into gambling, deception and disgrace.

Told by des Grieux himself, the novel is a passionate and painfully honest account of a love that overturns every principle. Prévost portrays both lovers with sympathy, and Manon, at once loving and faithless, remains one of the most fascinating heroines in French fiction.

Manon Lescaut appeared in 1731 as the last volume of Prévost's Memoirs and Adventures of a Man of Quality. In 1733 copies were seized in Paris for their immoral content, which only increased its popularity. This edition offers the original French text, an English translation by an unnamed translator and a Spanish translation by Antonio de Hoyos y Vinent.
books.author_short: French priest, novelist and translator (1697–1763), author of Manon Lescaut.
author_long: Antoine François Prévost d'Exiles, known as the Abbé Prévost, was born at Hesdin, in northern France, on 1 April 1697. He was a priest, novelist, journalist and translator, and led an adventurous life. He died on 25 November 1763.
His best-known work is the seven-volume Memoirs and Adventures of a Man of Quality (1728–1731), whose final volume is Manon Lescaut.

books.title: Taras Bulba
books.author: Nikolai Gogol
books.desc: An old Zaporozhian Cossack leader takes his two sons to war against the Poles, in Gogol's epic tale of courage, loyalty and fanaticism on the Ukrainian steppe.
about: The fierce old Cossack Taras Bulba welcomes home his sons Ostap and Andrii, back from their studies at the academy, and soon takes them to the Zaporozhian Sich, the camp of the free Cossacks on the Dnieper. When war breaks out against the Poles, father and sons ride out with the Cossack army and lay siege to the city of Dubno, where Andrii's feelings for a young Polish noblewoman set him against his own people.

Gogol's romantic, epic novella celebrates the wild freedom, comradeship and courage of the Cossacks while showing the violence and fanaticism of their wars. It also reflects the hostility of its time towards Poles and Jews, who are portrayed through harsh stereotypes.
Taras Bulba was first published in 1835 in the collection Mirgorod and revised in a longer version in 1842. This edition also contains other tales by Gogol, among them "The Cloak".
books.author_short: Russian writer born in Ukraine (1809–1852), author of Dead Souls, The Government Inspector and Taras Bulba.
author_long: Nikolai Gogol was born in 1809 in Sorochintsy, near Poltava, in Ukraine, then part of the Russian Empire. His Ukrainian stories, Evenings on a Farm near Dikanka (1831), quickly made him famous. After his comedy The Government Inspector was attacked in 1836, he lived abroad for most of the next twelve years. He died in Moscow on 4 March 1852.

Gogol blended fantasy, satire and realism in a way that deeply influenced Russian literature. Besides Taras Bulba, his best-known works include the play The Government Inspector (1836), the stories of St Petersburg such as "The Overcoat", and the novel Dead Souls, whose first part appeared in 1842.
